The paper explores how writing tools with large language models (LLMs) can reduce gender bias in hiring evaluations. The authors conducted a large-N, between-subjects experiment in which participants evaluated résumés from male and female job applicants using a writing tool with LLM-based autocomplete suggestions. The results showed that counter-stereotypical suggestions increased the perceived competence and likelihood of being selected as a trusted leader for female applicants, but activated gender backlash for male applicants. The authors believe that this paper could inspire new research questions and provide valuable insights for academic recommendation writers.
